- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% above recent mean), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–4% above peak for next 7–14 days.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.4) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; apply downward bias of 1–3% for 3–7 days after peak.
- When true price drops sharply (≥3% from prior day), model often lags; adjust forecast to match true drop by day +1 or +2.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.1–0.4) and price is near mean, model tends to oscillate; smooth forecast by averaging 3–5 prior values.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the period; reduce first 5–7 days’ forecast by 1–3% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment is consistently 0.00, model tends to overpredict; apply 3–5% downward correction for next 10 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day windows; if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
